lines.text: Welcome! Today you will meet your AI assistant, set it up safely, and write a real work email.
A chatbot like ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini is like a very well-read assistant.
It has read a huge amount of text and learned how words usually follow each other.
When you type a request, it predicts a helpful reply, word by word.
Google search finds web pages that already exist on the internet.
A chatbot writes a fresh answer every time, so it can sound confident and still be wrong.
Treat it like a smart new intern: fast and useful, but always checked.
Never paste passwords, Aadhaar or PAN numbers, bank details, or client and customer data.
Do not put confidential company files into a personal AI account.
Swap real details for placeholders like [Client name] or [Order no.].
Give the AI your rough note, say who the email is for, and ask for a polite tone.
Read the draft, fix anything that is wrong, and only then send it.
Your name is on it, so you are responsible for it.
You need just two free accounts to start, and having more is even better.
Every tool has a message box, a new chat button, and a settings page.
Open the settings once and look for the privacy or data controls, so you choose how your chats are used.
Free plans have limits, so keeping two tools ready means you are never stuck.
Here a shop owner pastes a rough note, with a placeholder instead of the real order number.
In seconds, Claude writes a clean and polite email with a subject line.
But look closely: the email promises delivery by 11 am, and the note never said that.
The AI filled a gap with a guess, so we delete that part before we send.
Now we paste the exact same prompt into Gemini to compare.
This version sticks to the facts in the note and does not add a made-up time.
Trying two tools takes one minute, and you simply keep the better draft.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
